title: Stopping a server must end its open connections before the quit path runs
rule: When a transport serves the API on a thread per connection (IPC pipe or socket, a raw TCP server), its stop must end every open connection and serve no request after it returns: record each connection with a handle that can close it from another thread (a dup'ed socket to shutdown, a duplicated pipe handle to DisconnectNamedPipe), refuse new connections and check the stop flag before every dispatch, and wait (bounded) for a request already running. Joining only the accept thread leaves detached connection threads dispatching after the quit path ended the session fonts, and on Windows a still-open server instance makes the next FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE bind fail. Test it with a client that stays connected across the stop: a request it sends afterwards gets no reply and changes nothing, and the same name binds again at once.
rationale: E29.1 (#182): IpcEndpoint::stop joined only the accept thread, so a plugin that kept its connection open could still activate a session font after CoreApi::shutdown, leaving an HKCU Fonts value after exit, and the Windows pipe could not be bound again after a cancelled update.
